headline: Prioritize access: login failures are the most severe actionable complaints per review
memo_markdown:
## Recommendation
Direct next quarter’s product effort to **access**, focused on reliable login and sign-in. This recommendation prioritizes the severity and core-task impact of access failures over the larger complaint volumes in billing/support and usability. Users unable to sign in may be blocked from using the service at all; the trade-off is choosing a smaller complaint pool over the largest total burden.

## Evidence
The clearest access signal is Login and Sign-In Problems: 6511 complaints (Claim 1), severity sum 26008 (Claim 2), and mean severity 3.99 (Claim 3). Its priority score is 26008 (Claim 4). The evidence is consistent with an essential task failing: typical review 5f959f21-cd36-4c4d-924d-0c4a345404dc says “I can't login even after putting correct password”. A second typical review, e225182d-9acf-487b-b7ab-95b7825f55ad, says “it won't login me again”.

The area-level figures reinforce the severity-per-complaint case: access has mean severity 3.98 and 10267 severity-4-or-5 complaints among 10732 complaints. Playback is the nearest alternative on mean severity at 3.68, but access has the highest area mean severity and its complaints center on entry to the service, rather than a particular playback experience.

## Alternatives considered
The strongest counter-argument is volume. Access ranks last in both complaint count and severity sum across the four candidate areas: billing/support has 62732 complaints and severity sum 185030, while usability has 69060 complaints and severity sum 180210. Those areas represent larger total burdens, so choosing access means forgoing broader volume reduction. Yet access’s area mean severity is 3.98, versus 2.95 for billing/support and 2.61 for usability; I would prioritize the more severe, potentially service-blocking issue over volume for this quarter. Playback also merits attention: its area mean severity is 3.68, with 43602 complaints and severity sum 160591. Its totals are substantial, but access has the higher mean severity.

Billing/support includes complaints about payment and feature restrictions; a high-severity example, which is a rare worst case rather than typical, is review 50d52e8a-94ca-4443-94ad-5e5a74aa7b47: “caused me to lose my current plan”. That is important, but the broad area mean is lower than access’s. Usability’s greater complaint count is a strong competing case, but its lower mean severity makes it a weaker choice under this criterion.

## Limitations
These are self-selected historical Google Play reviews from 17 May 2022 to 15 Nov 2023, not a representative measure of all users or current performance. Cancellation language is intent, not observed churn, and there is no revenue data; this memo makes no claim about revenue at risk or causal retention effects. Coverage reports 660609 completed, 0 pending, and 13 quarantined out of 660622 source rows, so the analyzed set is not the entire source. The largest issue, ISS-other-general, is generic dissatisfaction with no specific feature and is not an actionable product area. Severity may be inflated: on 50 hand-labeled golden reviews, model severity matched human labels 76% of the time, with errors almost always one level too high, so issue order is more reliable. Independent relabeling of 4842 sampled reviews agreed on topic, intent, and severity together 78% of the time. These uncertainties argue for validating login failures with product telemetry before finalizing scope.
